newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urged to seek code for alcohol ads.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urged to seek code for alcohol ads.

text.p: Under pressure from President Clinton to quit pitching hard liquor over the airwaves, the liquor industry Friday urged the president to bring together the beer, wine, broadcast and spirits industries to develop a common advertising code.

The Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, in a letter to Clinton, urged the president to ask the distillers, brewers and vinters together with the broadcasters to "come to the table" to develop and adopt a common code for alcohol ads within 90 days.
The initiative comes after Clinton on Tuesday asked the Federal Communications Commission to study ways to prevent the hard liquor industry from selling its products over television and radio.
The industry last year abandoned a decades-old voluntary ban on such promotions, and Clinton called on hard liquor executives to renew their moratorium.
The hard liquor industry's voluntary ban had been in effect for TV ads since 1948 and radio ads since 1936.

In an initial response to Clinton's calls, DISCUS said earlier this week it was unfair and inaccurate to draw a distinction between advertising for hard liquor and for beer and wine, whose ads were not covered by the voluntary ban and have run on TV for decades.
